Key Research Thinking Patterns: Multilevel Analysis: This researcher employs multilevel analysis to examine the relationship between chronic disease and e-cigarette/cigarette use from young adulthood to adulthood, considering the impact of chronic disease on smoking behavior (e.g., using the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health (Add Health)).

Structural Equation Modeling: The researcher utilizes structural equation modeling to investigate the factorial invariance of the Honor Ideology for Manhood (HIM) and Honor Ideology for Womanhood (HIW) scales across gender and ethnicity-based groups, and to examine the impact of feminine honor endorsement on intentions to seek catch-up HPV vaccinations among young adult women.

Machine Learning and Data Mining: This researcher applies machine learning and data mining techniques, such as Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), k-means algorithm, and Vector Autoregressive (VAR) models, to analyze intensive longitudinal data (ILDs) and identify clusters, and to perform joint variable selection in generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs).

Statistical Modeling: The researcher employs various statistical modeling techniques, including weighted multilevel logistic regression, confirmatory factor analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and sequential mediation analysis, to examine the relationships between variables and to identify the underlying structures of the data.
Summary Description: Hairong Song is a researcher with expertise in preventive medicine, public health, epidemiology, and psychology. Her primary focus is on understanding the relationships between chronic disease, tobacco use, and young adult health, as well as the impact of honor ideology on health behaviors. She employs a range of methodological approaches, including multilevel analysis, structural equation modeling, machine learning, and statistical modeling, to examine these relationships and identify effective interventions. Her work has significant implications for public health education and chronic disease prevention.
